events.title: Thomas Paine Publishes Common Sense
events.body: Paine's 47-page pamphlet argues for American independence in plain language accessible to ordinary readers. It sells approximately 100,000 copies in three months — the best-selling printed work per capita in American history — and transforms the political imagination of the colonies.

events.title: Gibbon: Decline and Fall of Rome Vol. I
events.body: Gibbon publishes the first volume of his magisterial history, tracing Rome from its height through the fall of Constantinople in 1453. Its sceptical treatment of Christianity shocks contemporaries; its prose and scope remain unmatched in English historical writing.

events.title: Adam Smith Publishes The Wealth of Nations
events.body: Smith publishes the foundational text of modern economics, arguing for free markets, the division of labour, and the 'invisible hand.' It provides the intellectual framework for industrial capitalism and remains the most influential work of economics ever written.

events.title: British Forces Evacuate Boston
events.body: After an 11-month siege, British forces evacuate Boston following Washington's fortification of Dorchester Heights with cannon from Fort Ticonderoga. The first significant American military success of the Revolutionary War shifts the war's focus southward.

events.title: The Illuminati Founded in Bavaria
events.body: Adam Weishaupt founds the Order of the Illuminati, advocating Enlightenment values including rationalism and separation of Church and State. Suppressed by the Bavarian government in 1785, its brief existence generates conspiracy theories that persist into the 21st century.

events.title: Watt's Steam Engine Gains Commercial Traction
events.body: Watt and Boulton's improved steam engine — with its separate condenser — begins transforming industry. Within a generation it powers cotton mills, iron foundries, and railways. It is the engine of the Industrial Revolution.

events.title: United States Declaration of Independence
events.body: The Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence, drafted primarily by Thomas Jefferson. It declares thirteen colonies free states, articulating natural rights and popular sovereignty. It remains one of the most influential political documents in history.
events.imageCredit: National Archives of the United States / Wikimedia Commons

events.title: Battle of Long Island
events.body: British forces decisively defeat Washington's Continental Army in the largest battle of the Revolution by troop numbers. Washington loses approximately 1,500 men but saves his army through a daring overnight retreat across the East River under cover of fog.

events.title: Nathan Hale Executed as a Spy
events.body: Nathan Hale, a 21-year-old schoolteacher and Continental Army captain, is executed by the British after being captured behind enemy lines. He reportedly said: 'I only regret that I have but one life to lose for my country.'

events.title: Washington Crosses the Delaware
events.body: Washington leads a daring overnight crossing of the ice-choked Delaware River on Christmas night, launching a surprise attack on Hessian forces at Trenton. The victory — at a cost of two American deaths from exposure — revives collapsing Revolutionary morale.
